turns.t: The booking says you had a urine dipstick done at your check-up, and it showed something. What did they tell you?
Well, the nurse did it and said there was protein in it, or a trace, I think. I didn't really follow what that means.
Okay. Before we get to the dipstick, has anything about your waterworks seemed different to you?
Hmm. Now you mention it, there's been a lot of froth when I go. Like bubbles on top, a bit like washing-up liquid.
Mm. Go on.
It's in the loo, the bubbles, and they hang around a while before they go. I thought it was just the toilet cleaner at first.
And how long have you noticed that?
About three weeks, I'd say. Maybe a bit longer, but I only started really looking recently.
Is it every time you pass water, or only now and then?
Most mornings, first thing. Less so later in the day. It's not every single time.
I see. Anything else about the water itself? Colour, smell, how often you go?
The colour's the usual straw sort of yellow. I go the normal amount, I think. Maybe once in the night.
Right.
Is it the kidneys, doctor? I keep reading things on my phone and it's put the wind up me.
It's worth taking seriously, but froth by itself is very common and has plenty of causes. That's why we measure it properly.
How do you measure it?
With a urine sample sent to the lab. It gives an exact figure for how much protein is leaking, rather than a trace on a stick.
Is that a different test from the one the nurse did?
Yes, much more precise. The stick is a quick screen, and the lab test tells us what to make of it.
Okay. And what happens if it does show protein?
Then we'd plan the next step together. I don't want to guess before we have the number.
Fair enough.
Does anyone in the family have trouble with their kidneys?
My dad did. He had kidney trouble in his sixties, and ended up seeing a specialist at the big hospital.
I see. That's useful for me to know.
Oh dear. Does that make it more likely I've got it too?
It means we're careful, that's all. It's one more reason to do the proper test and not shrug it off.
Right. Should I be eating differently or drinking more water in the meantime?
Drink as you normally would. No need to change anything until the results are in.
What about salt? My husband always says I put too much on my chips.
Tell him to wait for the results too. We can talk about salt once we know more.
Anything else going on with your health that you wanted to mention while you're here?
Not really. I had my gallbladder out about six years ago, but that was all sorted.
Good to know. Let me just feel your tummy, if you'd lie back on the couch for me.
Your abdomen feels soft and comfortable all over.
So that's all right then?
That part is. The answer will come from the urine test, so I'd like to arrange a urine protein test for you today.
Do I need to do anything special, like fast or collect it all day?
Just a first morning sample, since that's when you see the froth. Take the pot home, bring it back to the desk.
I can do that. And I'll ring you if the froth changes, will I?
Do ring the surgery if anything worries you. Otherwise, we'll contact you once the result is in.
Lovely, thank you for explaining it so clearly. I feel better for having come.

chief_complaint.value: there's been a lot of froth when I go

clinical_actions.description: Arrange urine protein test (first morning sample)
